issues.legal_issue: Whether special leave should be revoked when the applicant materially misstates a fact and misrepresents a publication as having been made under the court’s authority.
material_facts: The applicant stated that the sale proclamation did not say the property was being sold subject to a mortgage charge, although the proclamation contained such a note.
The applicant published a public notice captioned as a court notice, presenting it as though it had been published under the court’s orders.
issues.conclusion: The Court revoked the special leave, dismissed the appeal arising from it, and held that the stay already granted stood vacated.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the applicant’s material misstatement and its publication of a notice as though it had been issued under the Court’s orders as sufficient reasons to revoke special leave. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited.

predicates.special_leave_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding in which special leave has been granted for an appeal.
predicates.material_fact_misstated: The applicant stated a material fact that was contradicted by the relevant record.
predicates.false_court_authority_notice_published: The applicant published a notice in a way that represented it as having been issued under the court’s authority.

issues.definition: When a special-leave proceeding involves both a material misstatement by the applicant and a publication falsely presented as having court authority, special leave is revoked and the appeal is dismissed.
